faq.q: Does helping others make you happier?
faq.a: Yes. Studies show that being kind and helping others often makes the helper feel happier too, sometimes even more than treating themselves.
asks: Does being kind make you happy?

faq.q: Why does exercise make me feel good?
faq.a: When you move, your body releases chemicals like endorphins that lift your mood and ease stress. Playing outside in daylight helps even more.
asks: Why do I feel happy after sport?

faq.q: Does having more stuff make you happy?
faq.a: Only for a short time. People quickly get used to new things, so the happy feeling fades. Experiences and time with people usually give longer-lasting happiness.
asks: Will new toys make me happier?

faq.q: Should I be happy all the time?
faq.a: No. Nobody is happy all the time, and all feelings, like sadness and anger, are normal and useful. Happiness is about lots of good moments, not every moment.
asks: Is it bad that I am not always happy?

faq.q: What if I never feel happy anymore?
faq.a: If you have not felt happy or enjoyed things for weeks, talk to a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. You deserve support, and things can get better.

facts: The Harvard Study of Adult Development began in 1938 and has followed people for more than 80 years; it found that close relationships are strongly linked to a happy, healthy life.
In a 2008 study, people who spent money on others felt happier than people who spent the same money on themselves.
